anti_overlap: fd-spice-blending-flavor-axes covers axis interaction; this covers axis value geometry and distribution
decision_lens: Total light performance from facet arrangement — each facet must contribute to brilliance, fire, and scintillation without dead zones
distance_rationale: Lapidaries solve a geometric optimization problem about how many cuts at what angles maximize a multi-dimensional output — structurally identical to personality axis design.
expected_isomorphisms: Facet angles map to axis value ranges. Dead zones map to indistinguishable personality regions. Light performance (brilliance/fire/scintillation) maps to behavioral visibility. Yield tradeoff maps to axis count decision.
focus: How lapidaries design facet arrangements to maximize the interplay of light through a gem's geometry
name: fd-gem-cutting-facet
persona: Master lapidary specializing in custom facet designs, who understands how the angle and arrangement of each facet affects the total light performance of a gemstone
review_areas: Evaluate whether personality axes have 'dead zones' — facet angles that produce no internal reflection are wasted. Are there personality value ranges (e.g., 0.4-0.6) that produce no observable behavior?

Check the 'pavilion vs crown' distinction: gem facets serve different optical functions depending on position. Do the proposed axes serve different TYPES of behavioral function, or are they all doing the same kind of work?

Assess value distribution: lapidaries don't distribute facet angles uniformly — they cluster around key optical angles. Should personality values cluster at behaviorally interesting points rather than uniform random?

Evaluate the 'yield vs beauty' tradeoff: cutting more facets wastes more rough stone. Is 3 axes the right 'cut' for the behavioral 'rough' — or would 2 deep-cut axes produce more brilliance than 3 shallow ones?
Check for 'light leakage' — in gems, bad pavilion angles let light escape the bottom. In personality, bad axis design lets behavioral distinction 'leak' through — the player can't tell elves apart

severity_examples.condition: No bimodal or weighted distribution at generation
severity_examples.scenario: Uniform random distribution on each axis means 68% of elves cluster in the 0.3-0.7 range — like cutting a gem with random angles, most of the behavioral 'light' is lost

severity_examples.condition: All axes primarily modify social interaction rather than different behavioral domains
severity_examples.scenario: All 3 axes affect the same type of behavior (social dynamics) like facets all cut at the same angle — no optical diversity

success_hints: Each personality value produces visible behavioral 'light' — no dead zones, no wasted axes. The value distribution maximizes the variety of behavioral 'fire' across the colony.
task_context: The number and arrangement of personality dimensions is a design geometry problem — how many dimensions, at what values, to maximize behavioral distinction.
